_about: A made-up example for a tiny shop codebase (an api/ folder in Go). Copy the shape, not the words.

area:api.what: The part of the shop that answers web requests about orders.
area:api.does: main.go starts a small web server. Each web address has its own [[handler]] in handlers/.

api/main.go.does: Connects the /orders address to ListOrders, prints a start message and waits for requests on port 8080.

api/main.go#main.what: The first code that runs when the server starts.
api/main.go#main.does: Registers the /orders handler, prints where it is listening, then starts serving.

api/main.go#startMessage.what: Writes the line printed at start-up.
api/main.go#startMessage.does: Puts the port number into a short sentence.

api/handlers/orders.go.does: Loads the orders, labels each one and sends the labels back to the browser.

api/handlers/orders.go#ListOrders.does: Asks loadOrders for every order, then writes each order's label into the reply.

api/handlers/orders.go#loadOrders.does: Returns two sample orders written into the code (a real shop would read a database here).

api/handlers/orders.go#formatOrder.what: Turns an order into the short label shown in lists.
api/handlers/orders.go#formatOrder.example: An order with a total of 20 becomes 'big'.

glossary.handler: A function the web server runs when a request arrives at one web address.

tours.title: Someone asks for their orders
tours.intro: From the request to the reply

steps.text: The server started earlier and is waiting. A browser asks for /orders.
The server hands the request to ListOrders.
Each order is labelled 'big' or 'small', and the labels go back to the browser.

api/main.go#main.in: Nothing; it runs when the program starts.
api/main.go#main.out: A running web server on port 8080.

api/handlers/orders.go#ListOrders.out: A reply with one label per order.

steps.text: main.go starts the server and connects /orders to the orders handler.
When someone asks for /orders, orders.go loads the orders, labels them and replies.
